title: Doval in Malé: Indian Ocean Must Connect Nations, Not Divide Them
excerpt: At the 8th Colombo Security Conclave, NSA Ajit Doval called for deeper cooperation on maritime security and drug trafficking, and said India would give the grouping its fullest support.
body:
• National Security Adviser Ajit Doval addressed the 8th Colombo Security Conclave meeting of national security advisers in Malé, Maldives, on Wednesday, November 25.
  • He said the Indian Ocean must remain a space that connects nations rather than divides them, and called for sustained cooperation on maritime security, counter-terrorism and cyber security.
  • Doval flagged drug trafficking and drug money as a growing regional threat, saying India is sharing intelligence with Sri Lanka, the Maldives and other partners and wants to expand that work.
  • The conclave's six members — India, Bangladesh, Maldives, Mauritius, Sri Lanka and Seychelles — meet in Malé from November 24 to 26; the grouping now has its own secretariat and secretary general.

National Security Adviser Ajit Doval told Indian Ocean nations in Malé on Wednesday, November 25, that the seas they share must remain a space that connects nations rather than divides them, as he opened India's case for deeper regional security cooperation at the 8th meeting of national security advisers of the Colombo Security Conclave (CSC).

"We the littoral states of the Indian Ocean region share a common maritime space and are connected by civilisational heritage shaped over a long period of history," Doval said, according to ANI. He recalled that earlier generations had left a legacy in which the seas connected communities, and urged members to preserve that tradition: the heritage passed on should bind future generations together, "not divide them through these seas."

Drug money named as a rising threat

Doval named drug trafficking and the money behind it as a serious and growing threat to the region. India is sharing intelligence on drug trafficking with Sri Lanka, the Maldives and other partners, he said, and wants that collaboration expanded. He also warned that artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies will reshape conflict and cooperation, saying the region had reflected on yesterday's challenges and must now be ready for tomorrow's — including by sharing technology, best practices and experience.

A grouping that now has a secretariat

The Colombo Security Conclave was formed in November 2020. Doval noted that the grouping now has a secretariat and a secretary general, and he welcomed the adoption of the CSC Charter and the memorandum of understanding establishing the secretariat in August 2024. The conclave works across five pillars: maritime safety and security; countering terrorism and radicalisation; combating trafficking and transnational organised crime; cyber security and protection of critical infrastructure and technology; and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.

"For India, the Colombo Security Conclave represents the intersection of our neighbourhood-first outlook and the Mahasagar vision."

— Ajit Doval, National Security Adviser, as reported by ANI

Doval assured member states of India's full commitment and support in building the grouping's collective capacity against evolving security challenges, and thanked the Maldives for hosting the meeting.

On the sidelines

A day earlier, on November 24, Doval met Maldives Minister of Defence and National Service Hassan Rasheed on the sidelines of the meeting to discuss strengthening defence and security cooperation between India and the Maldives, the High Commission of India in the Maldives said. Member states also reviewed decisions from the 7th NSA-level meeting, held in New Delhi on November 20, 2025, and the Roadmap for Cooperation and Activities for 2025–2026, according to the Ministry of External Affairs, and noted progress on training and capacity-building across the five pillars.

The Malé meeting runs from November 24 to 26 and brings together India, Bangladesh, the Maldives, Mauritius, Sri Lanka and Seychelles, with Australia and Malaysia attending as observers. The conclave is India's principal security forum in the Indian Ocean, and its members have committed to continuing their partnership on humanitarian assistance and disaster relief alongside the harder security agenda.
